macro: US equity indices are mixed at midday with the SPX flat, Nasdaq up 38 basis points, R2K up 30 basis points, and the Dow down 43 basis points. Markets are in a holding pattern as investors watch UN diplomatic developments around Iran and the Middle East, with Brent crude off modestly near $100 on hopes for a Hormuz resolution and the partial resumption of Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline. Treasuries are pretty flat across the curve, while gold, silver, and bitcoin are all modestly lower.
rates_fed: Treasuries are largely unchanged across the curve with no major rate catalysts driving action today. There is no notable Fed commentary in this update. The macro backdrop is dominated by geopolitical energy dynamics rather than monetary policy.
market_outlook: The market is in a wait-and-see mode, with the major indices treading water. The directional lean is neutral-to-cautiously bullish on AI and tech into a dense catalyst window over the next 10 days — Zuckerberg's Meta Connect keynote Wednesday night, OpenAI DevDay on September 29th, and Micron earnings on September 30th. Watch those AI events as the key near-term catalysts.
bull_case: AI-related names are outperforming broadly as investor excitement builds into the Meta Connect keynote Wednesday night and subsequent catalysts including OpenAI DevDay and Micron earnings. Meta's Muse personal AI agent is seeing surging downloads, and Shopify's integration with Muse for agentic checkout expands the commercial ecosystem. Iran's reported offer to reopen Hormuz within seven days and the partial restart of Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline are easing energy concerns, which could reduce a key macro headwind. Housing and travel/leisure names are also showing relative strength, suggesting some underlying consumer resilience.
bear_case: Financials are broadly under pressure with banks, brokers, insurers, and asset managers all underperforming, which could signal broader caution on economic growth. Lab testing stocks Quest and LabCorp are getting hit hard on larger-than-expected CMS Medicare rate cuts, a reminder of regulatory risk across healthcare. Texas Governor Abbott's permit freeze on new data center projects adds a potential constraint on the AI infrastructure buildout, and SB Energy delaying its IPO on weak investor reception signals some sentiment cooling around the data center boom. THOR Industries' earnings miss and commentary about a difficult macro landscape adds a cautionary note on the consumer and industrial side.

company_items.summary: AutoZone reported fiscal Q4 EPS of $56.05 versus the Street at $54.03, but the beat was low quality — driven by tariff refunds adding 145 basis points to gross margins and a non-cash LIFO benefit adding another 105 basis points. Domestic comps came in at +1.6% versus the Street's +3.1%, though management noted positive sales linearity in the quarter, which is providing some comfort.

MillerKnoll posted solid fiscal Q1 EPS of 53 cents versus the Street at 36 cents, and critically the beat holds up even excluding tariff refunds — stripping out the 11-cent tailwind still leaves EPS at 42 cents, well above consensus. Guidance is mixed with fiscal 2027 sales trimmed but EPS outlook left unchanged.

THOR Industries missed fiscal Q4 EPS at 78 cents versus the Street at 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% versus the Street's 13.85%. Revenue came in at $2.311 billion, down 8.4% year-over-year but above the Street's $2.17 billion estimate, and management cited a difficult macro environment.

Meta's Muse personal AI agent is seeing surging downloads ahead of Zuckerberg's keynote at Meta Connect on Wednesday night. Shopify will allow Muse to complete purchases on its platform, expanding the agentic commerce ecosystem, while Amazon has blocked Muse from its site. Investor expectations are growing increasingly bullish into the event.

Shopify announced it will allow Meta's Muse personal AI agent to complete purchases on its e-commerce platform, positioning itself as a key enabler of agentic commerce. This follows Amazon's decision to block Muse, potentially giving Shopify a competitive advantage in the emerging AI shopping agent ecosystem.

Quest Diagnostics shares were hit Tuesday following new Medicare payment rates from CMS for lab services, with the rate reductions coming in larger than the market had anticipated. This is a sector-wide headwind also hitting LabCorp.

LabCorp shares are under pressure alongside Quest Diagnostics following CMS announcing Medicare lab service rate cuts that were steeper than expected. The move represents a direct hit to reimbursement revenue for both major lab testing firms.

Cognex announced it will acquire RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. The deal expands Cognex's footprint into the Physical AI and robotics perception space.

Viking Therapeutics reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, including 22% weight loss. The data keeps Viking competitive in the increasingly crowded but high-value obesity drug market.

On Holdings held its analyst meeting and outlined plans to achieve 2029 sales of at least CHF 5.6 billion versus the Street at CHF 5.4 billion, with EBITDA margins of 22% or better versus the Street's 21% estimate. The company also adopted a $1 billion buyback authorization, adding shareholder return credibility to the growth story.

AI and semiconductor-linked tech names outperforming as the market looks ahead to Meta Connect, OpenAI DevDay, and Micron earnings. Housing names showing strength. Travel and leisure names also outperforming. Consumer staples catching a bid. Texas Governor Abbott's data center permit freeze adds a cloud over the AI infrastructure buildout narrative. Fertilizer stocks facing headwinds as Belarus downplays any potash deal with the White House.

tts_summary: Here is your midday market update for Tuesday September 22nd. Markets are doing essentially nothing at the moment — the S&P 500 is flat, the Nasdaq is up about 38 basis points, the Russell 2000 is up 30 basis points, and the Dow is lagging, down 43 basis points. Treasuries are flat across the curve. Brent crude is just under $100, off slightly, as there are some early diplomatic signals around Iran — reports suggest Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US takes initial steps to ease military pressure. Saudi Arabia is also signaling its East-West Pipeline may be partially coming back online, which is capping oil's upside. The market is essentially in a holding pattern waiting on geopolitics and a very dense AI catalyst window coming up over the next ten days. On the company side, AutoZone beat on earnings but the quality of that beat is questionable — tariff refunds and a non-cash inventory accounting item drove most of the upside, and domestic comparable sales missed at positive 1.6 percent versus the Street's 3.1 percent. Stock is rallying anyway on positive sales linearity commentary. MillerKnoll was a genuinely clean beat — 53 cents versus 36 cents expected, and the company would have beaten even stripping out the tariff refund benefit. THOR Industries disappointed, missing on the bottom line with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year, and management called out a tough macro environment. Viking Therapeutics reported 22 percent weight loss data from its GLP-1 drug trial, keeping it in the conversation in the obesity space. Cognex is buying RealSense for roughly 500 million dollars upfront, expanding into Physical AI and robotic perception. On Holdings raised its long-term targets above Street estimates and added a billion-dollar buyback. On the negative side, Quest Diagnostics and LabCorp are both getting hit on CMS Medicare rate cuts for lab services that came in larger than expected — that is a real reimbursement headwind for the sector. Meta is the key name to watch into Wednesday night — Muse downloads are surging, Shopify is integrating the agent for agentic checkout, and Zuckerberg's keynote is shaping up as the biggest near-term catalyst for AI sentiment broadly. After that comes OpenAI DevDay on the 29th and Micron earnings on the 30th. Directionally, the market is neutral-to-cautiously bullish on AI into that catalyst window, but financials broadly lagging and the data center permit freeze in Texas are worth watching as potential friction points. Stay close to the Meta keynote Wednesday night — that is the most important event this week.
